adjudication_rationale: The GGUF dequantize ABI truncated large element counts and could leave output uninitialized, a generic memory-safety flaw. Sides with coder B.
ROCm AITER advertised an incompatible CUDA-graph mode and caused OOM/accuracy issues; full ROCm AITER serving capture is primary. Sides with coder B.
The FlashInfer availability check could not be traced by torch.dynamo in a compiled FusedMoE serving configuration. Sides with coder B.
The PR avoids unnecessary FP8 MLA metadata work and presents benchmark validation, but does not establish a correctness, crash, or severe availability failure. Sides with coder B.
Padded hidden dimensions made FusedMoE copy original-size checkpoint tensors into padded parameters, a direct alignment edge. Sides with coder A.
Token-budget exhaustion could schedule new Mamba requests as decode and read stale SSM state; varying batch/token schedules is the key detector. Sides with coder A.
The ROCm-only Triton MXFP8 quantizer used the wrong exponent and existing ROCm reference tests would fail if run. Sides with coder A.
The fused KDA verify kernel wrote state read by later V tiles, creating schedule-dependent output variance rather than a hardware-only bug. Sides with neither coder.
The Mamba radix cache bug appeared at page_size=128 and escaped a loose KL threshold, so page-size edge tests with tight checks are appropriate. Sides with coder A.
Qwen3-Next MTP serving broke in GDN CUDA-graph metadata/stride handling, best caught by the full spec-decode serving matrix. Sides with coder B.
The AITER MLA decode gate omitted nhead=64 for the AMD TP2 DeepSeek-R1 path, causing memory faults. Sides with neither coder.
The record describes reducing CUDA graph stream count with no numeric change and no concrete severe availability failure. Sides with coder B.
The evidence establishes a missing Python attribute in DeepEPMoE but not a kernel-rooted correctness or dispatch failure. Sides with coder B.
The NVFP4 EP path left scale rows uninitialized when expert maps skipped physical rows, causing NaN scaling. Sides with coder B.
The modelopt compatibility note lacks a visible crash, wrong output, or kernel-specific root cause. Sides with coder B.
The record only has an empty body and the subject about NVFP4 online scale with pcg, so it lacks enough evidence. Sides with coder B.
The KV-cache JIT path selected kernels from the wrong dtype for int32/int64 indices and broke CI; dtype-matrix tests would catch it. Sides with coder A.
Attention backends supported BF16 KV cache but rejected the valid TRITON_MLA configuration at serving startup. Sides with coder A.
The EPLB/Waterfill record implies expert layout changes but does not show a concrete incorrect behavior or severe performance failure. Sides with neither coder.
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT produced a FlashAttention MLA scheduler_metadata shape RuntimeError in a serving benchmark. Sides with coder B.
ROCm AITER RMSNormQuantFusion used the wrong attention attribute for Kimi-Linear and crashed model startup. Sides with coder A.
The NVFP4 SiluMul fusion used an approximate sigmoid and only realistic online evaluation exposed the accuracy drop. Sides with coder B.
The record frames the change as a possible Hopper performance-regression workaround without a concrete correctness or severe availability failure. Sides with coder B.
The Marlin kernel had a read-write race causing corrupted output/NaNs, found by compute-sanitizer racecheck. Sides with neither coder.
The fusion matcher broke VL models in compiled FP8/fused paths, requiring model-level compile/e2e coverage. Sides with coder A.
The naive all2all path used dispatched instead of original hidden states for shared experts, which a backend/reference MoE test can expose. Sides with coder B.
DSV3 AWQ accuracy loss was attributed to fp16 overflow, requiring value distributions that exceed fp16 safety. Sides with coder A.
WNA16 LoRA could not select the correct modular MoE kernel after refactoring; targeted serving plus selection tests are plausible. Sides with neither coder.
Hopper defaults to FA3, which cannot support ALiBi, so Hopper ALiBi coverage would have caught the bad backend selection. Sides with coder B.
The TPU Pallas block-size logic caused VMEM estimation/OOM issues in TPU CI; TPU matrix coverage is primary. Sides with neither coder.
